summary: George Baumann is an Indologist who earned his PhD from Heidelberg University (~1968–1973) and studied at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen (~1973–1975). He held posts at the University of Tübingen (~1975–2001) and Tübingen University Library (1976–2001).

George Cardona is an Indologist and linguist who studied at NYU, Yale, and under Paul Thieme, Warren Cowgill, and several traditional teachers. He was a fellow at CASBS (1971–1972) and held a professorship at the University of Pennsylvania (~1965–2009).

George Chemparathy was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1961–1966) and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and served as professor at Utrecht University (~1972–1993).

George Cowgill was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Harvard University (~1956–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1964–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2018).

George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London (~1862–1863). He held an academic post at University College London from ~1866 to 1892.

George Cœdès was a scholar of archaeology, linguistics, and Indology who studied at EPHE and Humboldt University. He served as director of the EFEO (1929–1947), headed the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929), and curated the Musée d'Ennery (1947–1969).

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968–1972) and studied at the University of Sri Lanka. He served as Professor of Religion at Northwestern University (~1974–2012).

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago (1902) and Harvard University (1903–1905). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George E. Dunkel is a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins (1975–1978), Princeton (1978–1986), and the University of Zurich (appointed 1986).

George Foot Moore was a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale and Union Theological Seminary. He was a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and held professorships in theology and history of religion at Harvard University (1902–1928).
George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who studied at Phillips Academy (~1856–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He held a academic post at Harvard University from ~1870 to 1913.

George L. Hart is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1964–1971). He taught Sanskrit at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1975) and served as professor at UC Berkeley (~1975–2013).

George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at MIT and Indiana University (PhD ~1962–1966). He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969) and served as a linguistics professor at UC Berkeley from 1972 to 2016.

George Melville Bolling was a linguist and Indologist who earned a doctorate from Johns Hopkins (~1893–1897). He held posts at the Catholic University of America (1895–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1939), and served as LSA president in 1931.
George R. Elder is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University, where he completed doctoral work supervised by Alex Wayman (attested 1978).

George Rupp is a scholar of religious studies who was educated at Princeton, Yale Divinity School, and Harvard Divinity School. He held major posts at Rice University (1985–1993) and Columbia University (~1993–2002).
George Saintsbury was educated at King's College School and Merton College (~1863–1868). He held a post at the University of Edinburgh from ~1895 to 1915.

George Santayana was a philosopher who earned his PhD at Harvard under William James (~1888–1890) and studied at Berlin and Cambridge. He was a member of the philosophy faculty at Harvard University from 1907 to 1912.
George Sessions was a scholar in the field of philosophy. He held academic posts at Sierra College in 1992–1993 and in 2002.
George Shirt was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1864 and studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (~1864–1866).
